rule: GOAL: Fill four slots to match the top color sequence. CONTROLS: Click bottom colors to select, click slots to place. RULE: Placing a color swaps it with the slot’s gray dot. TRAP: Clicking slots without a selected color wastes actions.

GOAL: Reach the exit by navigating a grid of walls and open spaces. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Movement is discrete; each press advances exactly one cell, stopping only at walls. TRAP: Assuming arrows cause long slides like ice puzzles wastes time; they do not.

GOAL: Align the gray shape's stepped edges with the yellow door. CONTROLS: Click blue buttons to shift the gray boundary horizontally. RULE: Each click moves the top edge left and the bottom edge right by four units. TRAP: Assuming blue buttons act independently; they actually control a linked, opposing movement of the shape.

GOAL: Move the square to the target circle. CONTROLS: Clicking nearby dots moves the square one step toward them. RULE: The square must land directly on the circle to win. TRAP: Believing you must click every single dot individually, wasting moves on inefficient small hops instead of planning direct paths.

GOAL: Slide the green handle into the wall gap by aligning bands. CONTROLS: Top buttons shift upper band edges; bottom buttons shift lower band edges near each wall. RULE: Shared band boundaries move oppositely when linked buttons are pressed. TRAP: Clicking one button alone wastes moves; paired buttons must be balanced to isolate specific band shifts.

GOAL: Position the bar so falling blocks land precisely in both side notches without spilling. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar; Space drops the block. RULE: Blocks split at bar ends, creating two children that fall just outside the bar’s width. TRAP: Centering the bar causes spills; offset it so children align with notches, not the center.

GOAL: Navigate from the start to the exit while avoiding a directional trap. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The trap attacks only when you enter its specific firing line, not when you stand directly on it. TRAP: Assuming the trap is lethal everywhere is wrong; standing on its home cell is safe, allowing you to bypass it.

GOAL: Place all loose boxes into the highlighted target frames. CONTROLS: Arrows move the sprite; Space absorbs a glowing box or drops the carried one. RULE: You must walk into a box to make it glow before pressing Space to pick it up. TRAP: Assuming you can grab a box from any side; you must approach from directly below to trigger the glow.

GOAL: Fit the marker through the narrow channel into the left handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the marker and rotate its pattern; keypad actions shrink it. RULE: The marker must shrink to two rows to pass the gap. TRAP: Thinking rotation was the puzzle ignored the size constraint blocking the path.

GOAL: Guide the marker upward through a narrow gap into the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the marker; pressing UP twice cleared the level. RULE: The marker must align precisely with the gap to pass through. TRAP: Assuming the marker fits anywhere in the wide block wastes time; alignment is strict.

GOAL: Navigate from the bottom right to the bottom center while avoiding three stationary traps that fire along their facing lines. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move two spaces at a time, allowing you to jump over walls and trap danger zones. RULE: Traps are safe to land on only if you do not approach them head-on, meaning your direction must not oppose their facing. TRAP: Assuming all cells in front are safe if you are farther than two spaces away, when only the immediate two cells are dangerous.

GOAL: Align five colored bands so each handle sits exactly in its wall gap. CONTROLS: Clicking between walls shifts two units of white space from the left band to the right band. RULE: Handles plug gaps when the white level starts one row below the opening. TRAP: Assuming strict minimum bounds blocked moves; loose limits allowed efficient routing without dead ends.

GOAL: Align five glyph pairs by matching a shared rotational symmetry rule. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selection cursor; UP rotates the active glyph set. RULE: Blue and partner glyphs must share the exact same rotational pose to lock. TRAP: Assuming visual similarity implies correctness; identical looks can stem from different underlying rotations.

GOAL: Move the Y-shape to overlap the target circle. CONTROLS: Click a spot to shift the piece, keeping the clicked spot within five steps of the current shape. RULE: Each click moves the piece up to five rows and columns in any direction. TRAP: Assuming you can jump across gaps; clicks must stay close to the piece’s current position.

GOAL: Make the ball drop by turning all five glyphs black. CONTROLS: Click glyph parts to flip colors; click the ball’s edge to run the sequence. RULE: Black glyphs command the ball to move downward. TRAP: Clicking the ball’s center registers as no action; you must hit the top edge.

ESTABLISHED: The rod extends horizontally, pushing aligned blocks rightward in a fixed chain. FAILED: Extending without first clearing the rightmost block’s path causes a hard stop. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the far wall or maximizing rod length. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the head; Space extends the rod, dragging covered blocks until they hit obstacles or the limit.

GOAL: Shrink the tall marker to fit through a narrow gap and reach the pink socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker; clicking panel dots entered a sequence to trigger size changes. RULE: The marker only shrinks if the correct dot pattern is completed while positioned near the obstruction. TRAP: Assuming the marker could pass the gap in its original size or that the pattern worked from any location.

GOAL: Arrange letters to match a hidden slot order, clearing Level 2 in three actions. CONTROLS: Clicks swapped tile positions; Space submitted the current arrangement. RULE: A flash at a specific ring confirmed the letter matched that slot's order. TRAP: Assuming a failure meant the slot's order was wrong, rather than just the letter being incorrect.

GOAL: Fill the red pipe slots and green or blue boxes with the correct palette colors. CONTROLS: Click a palette color, then click a slot to place it; press space to submit. RULE: Pipe colors above determine which box below connects to that pipe position. TRAP: Assuming slots are random; they follow a specific left-to-right sequence across the red row and side boxes.

GOAL: Reach the exit while dodging a patrolling hazard. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step; each press advances time. RULE: The hazard moves every turn; you must stay in its path's gaps. TRAP: Believing you can dash through; oscillating to wait for the right timing was necessary.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens to match the target sequence Y R N b M O p. CONTROLS: Click palette items to place them in box slots, then press Space to verify. RULE: The green ring acts as a pipe, splitting the red box into left and right sections that read before and after the green box. TRAP: Assuming the pre-filled N could be moved; it is fixed, forcing the pipe into the third red slot to align the sequence.

GOAL: Rotate each cell's wheel to match the top reference pairs. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between cells; UP rotates the current wheel. RULE: Process cells left-to-right, rotating until the glyph pose matches the static target. TRAP: Assuming all target poses exist in every wheel; some cells lack the correct rotation entirely.

GOAL: Place two separate pieces into their matching circles to finish the level. CONTROLS: Clicking a destination moves the piece toward it, advancing one hop per click. RULE: You can only move a piece if it is currently on the board and not already placed. TRAP: Thinking you could move a piece that had already landed in a circle; once placed, it is locked.

GOAL: Decode the hidden sequence by rotating blue glyphs until their shapes match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selection cursor across the blue strip; cycling actions rotated the selected glyph. RULE: Each glyph had to match the target shape after a specific rotation, not just pixel count. TRAP: Assuming symmetry meant any rotation worked; distinct orientations mattered, wasting time on false matches.

GOAL: Align the yellow cross center to the grid intersection to cover all scattered dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cross; spacebar triggers the final confirmation or reset. RULE: The cross arms extend infinitely until hitting the board edge, covering any dot they touch. TRAP: Assuming the cross stops at the first dot or frame; it actually passes through, merging the dot into the beam.

GOAL: Collect the green gem at the bottom-right corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one space per press. RULE: Moving costs one action, but enemies always move regardless of your actions. TRAP: Believing overlapping enemies appear as separate items on the board, causing false mismatches.

GOAL: Align three blocks in a row by extending and retracting the rod to shift them into place. CONTROLS: Arrows extend or retract the rod, pushing or pulling any contiguous chain of blocks attached to its tip. RULE: Only blocks directly connected to the rod's tip move; others stay put, allowing you to isolate and shift specific segments. TRAP: Assuming the rod pushes all blocks in its path; it only moves the contiguous chain touching the tip, leaving gaps unaffected.

GOAL: Transform the input strip of shapes into the output strip by following hidden translation rules. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the editing cursor along the bottom row to place the correct final shapes. RULE: Shapes convert in two steps: first from source to middle color, then from middle to target color. TRAP: Trying to map source shapes directly to target shapes fails because no single-step rule exists.

GOAL: Center the purple square precisely inside the purple ring to complete the level. CONTROLS: Clicking a piece swaps its position with the other piece, allowing indirect movement. RULE: The square’s center is the midpoint between the two diamond pieces, so their positions must average to the ring’s location. TRAP: Believing clicking a piece moves it directly; actually, it swaps places, requiring two clicks to reposition a specific diamond.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to position the yellow block into the highlighted slot. CONTROLS: The left arrow shifts blocks counterclockwise; the right arrow shifts them clockwise. RULE: Each arrow click moves every block one step in its indicated direction around the perimeter. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the cursor; they actually rotate the entire ring relative to the fixed slot.

GOAL: Reduce the five scattered pegs to a single survivor by jumping over neighbors. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a valid landing spot to jump and remove the jumped piece. RULE: Jumps must land on empty spaces; blocked pegs cannot move or be jumped, so plan ahead to avoid stranding pieces. TRAP: Assuming distant pegs remain independent; they often become dead weight if not connected early, wasting moves that could save the game.

GOAL: Cover three red dots using rotating shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows moved shapes; SPACE cycled their form. RULE: Shapes must align perfectly with dots upon final placement. TRAP: Assuming shapes stayed static; ignoring the rotation cycle caused misalignment.

GOAL: Match the large grid to the small pattern shown beside it. CONTROLS: Click any cell to switch its color between red and blue. RULE: White cells in the pattern mean red; gray cells mean blue. TRAP: Assuming the pattern rotates or changes when you click; it stays fixed as the target.

GOAL: Align both colored dots with their respective cross centers simultaneously. CONTROLS: Click side panels to extend or retract the light beams, moving the dots along the grid lines. RULE: Victory triggers only when both dots occupy their target center points at the exact same moment. TRAP: Assuming a single dot reaching the center solves the level; it must wait for the other dot to align.

GOAL: Replicate the mini-panel's pattern onto the main grid. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color through the available palette. RULE: Mini colors are inverses of grid colors; match the mini's arrangement by painting the opposite shades. TRAP: Assuming the mini's center color belongs to the grid; it is a marker, not a target cell color.

GOAL: Move the two yellow markers into the specific target frames. CONTROLS: Red buttons shift items one way along the paths; green buttons reverse that movement. RULE: Each button rotates items along a fixed loop, so pressing the opposite color undoes the last move. TRAP: Thinking green buttons move items in a new direction; they actually just reverse the red button’s effect.

GOAL: Rotate the block to form a T-shape, then push it into the target box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; entering the cross triggers rotation. RULE: Stepping on the cross rotates the block, changing its shape to match the lock. TRAP: Believing the block stays the same shape; failing to rotate it prevents entry.

GOAL: Match overlapping 3x3 patterns from four mini grids onto the main board. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle colors; click minis to rotate their view. RULE: Where multiple minis cover a cell, their predicted colors must match perfectly. TRAP: Assuming minis align without rotation or offset; early clicks wasted time ignoring rotation mechanics.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover eight hidden dots using precise geometry. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide pieces; Space locks their final position. RULE: Shapes are fixed-size masks; only the endpoint matters, not the path taken. TRAP: Believing moving over a dot counts; only the final resting place provides coverage.

GOAL: Place yellow and orange blocks into matching static frames on two connected rings. CONTROLS: Left and right red buttons rotate each ring clockwise. Green buttons rotate counter-clockwise. RULE: Rotating one ring shifts blocks on the shared cells, moving blocks on both rings simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming blocks move independently. They share cells, so moving one block often drags the other, forcing complex coordinated sequences.

GOAL: Raise the green block to the top gap, then extend it down to the center. CONTROLS: Click right side of boxes to extend color bars. RULE: Extend the base sky first to lift everything, then widen yellow, then drop green. TRAP: Extending green before lifting causes it to hit the purple ceiling and block progress.

GOAL: Match each mini's ring to the surrounding grid cells. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color through the available palette. RULE: The ring symbol 'W' matches the mini's center color; 'g' matches any other color. TRAP: Assuming 'g' always means the base background color, rather than simply "not the center color."

GOAL: Guide the yellow and orange tokens to their matching colored targets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift entire rows or columns in a loop. RULE: Edges wrap around, so pushing off one side reappears on the opposite side. TRAP: Assuming a single continuous loop for each row or column; the wrap actually swaps positions between parallel tracks.

ESTABLISHED: Two blue blocks start at the bottom of a black arch. Moving right places them side-by-side at the top bar without triggering a win. The target area above is not black. FAILED: Simply positioning the blocks adjacent to each other at the top. Attempting to bridge the color boundary at the top bar. Moving blocks into the upper pipe section. GOAL IS NOT: Getting blocks to the top row. Making the blocks touch. Connecting the yellow and orange zones visually. Filling the entire black shape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide blocks until they hit walls or other blocks. There is no push mechanic

GOAL: Guide the blue block into the ring’s center by using a recorded ghost to hold a door open. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; Space records your moves and spawns a ghost that replays them. RULE: The ghost is solid and can press buttons, but it only repeats your exact path. TRAP: Believing the ghost would stop at the button; it keeps moving unless you record a path that parks it there.

GOAL: Guide the orange X to the green paint zone without touching the magenta swatch. CONTROLS: Arrows move the character; space resets the color state or confirms action. RULE: Only the final color source touched determines the character's final hue. TRAP: Assuming the gray frame paints the character; only the core swatch applies color.

GOAL: Trace a hidden twenty-one cell loop to position two yellow blocks over two fixed frame cells. CONTROLS: Clicks shifted contents along two distinct cycles, one long and one short, sharing five top cells. RULE: Content moves to the next cell in the cycle, wrapping around the end to the start. TRAP: Assuming the top row formed a separate, isolated loop instead of sharing cells with the main path.

ESTABLISHED: Two pieces exist, currently separated by distance. A two-block wall blocks direct pathing. Action budget is critically low. FAILED: Simple movement toward the opposite piece without contact did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving one piece to a specific coordinate or room entrance. CONTROLS: Clicking swaps piece positions. Arrow keys move the selected piece one block per press until blocked.

GOAL: Align the plug’s red tips with the green socket’s red markers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the white plug one grid step in the chosen direction. RULE: The plug’s left bar is 3 wide by 15 tall, matching the socket’s exact dimensions for a perfect fit. TRAP: Assuming the prongs must enter the hole; they cannot pass through the solid green block, only the side bar fits.

GOAL: Transform the grid into a specific checkerboard pattern using limited clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell flips it and its orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Parity constraints from hints uniquely determine the target pattern. TRAP: Assuming a simple flip logic was incorrect; the neighbor toggle rule required precise parity tracking to avoid invalid states.

GOAL: Lift the piece into the ring. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; clicks swap which piece is active. RULE: Clicking swaps control markers only, leaving pieces in place. TRAP: Clicking might seem to swap piece positions, but it only swaps the active dot.

GOAL: Align the charcoal block with the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece opposite to the input direction. RULE: Pressing LEFT shifts the piece RIGHT; press DOWN to lower it. TRAP: Assuming inputs match movement direction leads to hitting walls.

GOAL: Fill the row with M, Y, pipe, pipe, p and the box with N, R, R to match the sequence. CONTROLS: Click a palette item, then click a slot to place it. RULE: The box reads left to right, so the single N must sit in the leftmost slot. TRAP: Assuming the two pipes can go anywhere; they must be adjacent to satisfy the pattern.

GOAL: Align the reflected mirror piece with the yellow target using only horizontal shifts. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows move the central divider line; Up, Down, and Space do nothing in this stage. RULE: Moving the divider one step shifts the mirror two steps, doubling your horizontal reach. TRAP: Trying to move pieces vertically or rotating them wastes time; only the divider’s position matters here.

GOAL: Route colored rings into the central red box to unlock matching color sequences in the side boxes. CONTROLS: Click a palette item, then click a target slot to place it; press Space to submit your solution. RULE: The position of each ring in the red box dictates which side box fills which segment of the final pattern. TRAP: Ignoring the pre-filled rings in side boxes leads to impossible placements; always match those first to find the correct ring order.

GOAL: Move the 2x2 knob to the yellow core. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the knob two cells; clicks toggle platform colors. RULE: The knob only stands on matching colors; toggle platforms to create a path. TRAP: Thinking arrows move one cell wastes time; they always move two.

GOAL: Route colored rings through three stacked boxes to match a target sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items to fill box slots, then press Space to run the flow. RULE: Rings pass vertically between boxes, but each box reads its contents strictly left to right. TRAP: Assuming vertical pipes dictate the order; actually, horizontal position within each box determines sequence priority.

GOAL: Align all eight rotating glyph tiles to match fixed slot patterns. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; up pressed the current tile to cycle its glyphs. RULE: Each slot demanded a specific glyph order, requiring precise alignment per position. TRAP: Assuming tiles could be solved independently without checking the fixed global order caused wasted rotations.

GOAL: Guide three yellow blocks from the outer ring into the central triangular frame. CONTROLS: Click outer rings to rotate a block’s direction; click outward arrows to move it one step away; click the center to swap ring positions. RULE: Each click moves a block one step in its current direction, so rotate before pushing to hit the target. TRAP: Rotating too many times wastes moves; always check the shortest path between directions.

GOAL: Align the divider so reflections of the pieces cover the upper targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece or divider; Space cycles selection between them. RULE: The divider acts as a mirror axis; reflections depend on its vertical position. TRAP: Assuming pieces must touch targets directly ignores the reflection mechanic and the divider’s role.

ESTABLISHED: The player can rise to the upper room. The pink cross shape is located on the ceiling of this room, directly left of the landing spot. FAILED: Staying in the lower room or moving right yields no progress. Previous attempts to reach the cross from below failed. GOAL IS NOT: The cross is not a wall or a hazard that repels the player. It is not located in the starting area. CONTROLS: RIGHT moves right. MOUSE clicks coordinates to trigger jumps. LEFT moves left.

GOAL: Navigate the character to the pink cross target located at the far end of the upper corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the character horizontally; clicking the mouse triggered the upward lift mechanism. RULE: The lift only activated when standing directly on the designated pressure pad at the bottom of the shaft. TRAP: Assuming the cross was a hazard caused hesitation; it was actually the exit goal.

GOAL: Slide pieces to align red connectors and form a closed loop. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; clicks select a piece. RULE: Pieces pass through each other; only red ends must touch to lock. TRAP: Avoided moving pieces simultaneously; one wrong move causes a gridlock requiring many undo steps.

ESTABLISHED: Stamping purple upright failed. The stack currently holds purple with a white top section. FAILED: Matching the panel pattern exactly did not trigger a win. Rotating and stamping without changing the piston color had no effect. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the visual panel pattern on the stack. CONTROLS: Left rotates the piston. Space stamps the current color. Clicking selects the piston color.

GOAL: Align three separate blocks to fill the yellow outline. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space switches selection between blocks. RULE: Pieces pass through each other freely, so overlap is allowed during movement. TRAP: Moving the wide block before the tall one creates a collision that wastes moves.

GOAL: Align yellow pieces into their target slots to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows rotate rows and squares; blue arrows shift columns. RULE: Opposing arrows act as inverses on disjoint cycles; shared cells link different groups. TRAP: Assuming all moves affect a single loop wastes time; recognize independent cycles sharing one cell.

GOAL: Guide the knob to the hidden socket to reveal the red toggle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicking plugs rotates bars. RULE: Knob contact with the socket unlocks the next switch. TRAP: Assuming all switches are visible; the red toggle only appears after the socket is pressed.

GOAL: Place the unrotated P piece onto the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection between the piece and mirror dividers. RULE: The piece must match the unflipped copy to fit the specific yellow pattern. TRAP: Believing the piece could rotate wastes moves; it must be placed in its original orientation.

GOAL: Move the knob from the socket to the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicks rotate colored bridges. RULE: Only bridges matching the knob's current orientation support it. TRAP: Rotating a bridge under the knob causes a fall; always move the knob off first.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks to clear a path for the sky to reach the purple target. CONTROLS: Clicking a color extends or retracts its block in a specific direction. RULE: Blocks must slide past each other without overlapping; order matters to avoid collisions. TRAP: Assuming you can move blocks in any order; premature moves cause permanent blockages.

GOAL: Fit pieces into matching rings. CONTROLS: Arrows moved pieces three spaces; clicks selected them. RULE: Match piece size to the ring's interior dimensions. TRAP: Assuming one arrow press equals one grid space caused overshooting and wasted time.

GOAL: Guide the Z-shape into the designated slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece; rotation keys spin it. RULE: Pieces cannot pass through each other, requiring precise pathing. TRAP: Assuming overlap is allowed wasted moves; checking collisions first saves actions.

GOAL: Arrange two mirror-image shapes to fill the target zone exactly without overlapping. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the selected piece; Space cycles between the piece and the axis divider. RULE: The divider acts as a mirror; moving it changes where reflected pieces land relative to the original. TRAP: Assuming pieces can pass through each other; they block movement if paths intersect, requiring careful order.

GOAL: Fit four puzzle pieces into the grid to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move pieces; clicking selects them; the space bar rotates the active piece. RULE: Pieces snap into place automatically once their connectors align with the matching sockets. TRAP: Assuming rotation keeps the piece’s top-left corner fixed; it actually pivots around the center, shifting the anchor point.

GOAL: Reach the green exit while navigating a maze filled with hazards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Stepping onto a trap destroyed it, allowing safe passage on subsequent visits. TRAP: Assuming destroyed traps remained blocked walls, causing unnecessary detours and wasted moves.

GOAL: Reach the far green tile on the right, bypassing a wall in the middle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one space in the pressed direction. RULE: Moving into a trap destroys it only if you do not enter head-on. TRAP: Assuming you must dodge every trap; sometimes stepping into one from the side clears the path.

GOAL: Guide the blue avatar to the exit while two ghost clones simultaneously hold two separate pressure plates to open doors. CONTROLS: Arrows move the avatar and record its path; Space saves the current recording into a slot and advances the pointer. RULE: Only two ghost slots are active; writing to the third slot wipes all previous ghosts and resets the cycle. TRAP: Believing you can store three ghosts; the third save clears the board instead of adding a helper.

ESTABLISHED: Cup needs four ups. Program lacks up. Row one mappings match level one. Boxes rotate shadow, not cup. FAILED: Box clicks changed notch pose but not cup orientation or position. No win from notch alignment. GOAL IS NOT: Aligning shadow to arch. Moving goal marker independently. CONTROLS: Row one buttons move piece down, left, right. No up. Box clicks rotate notch only.

ESTABLISHED: The bar keeps its position between tests, allowing cheap iteration. The block rises when unsupported. FAILED: Moving the bar to columns 24, 32, 36, 40, and 44 at rows 36-39 caused no completion. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the bar with the block's column range at the starting height triggers a win. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the persistent bar. SPACE runs the simulation, which may kill the player or fail silently.

GOAL: Move the first piece to its target slot by navigating around the bottom bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; Space selects the next piece or divider. RULE: Selecting a piece turns its internal holes white, allowing you to track its exact position visually. TRAP: The piece merges with the bottom bar if it touches it, making component tracking fail; rely on the white hole markers instead.

GOAL: Clear the board by removing all pegs through jumping. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the platform; clicking a peg selects it for movement or jumping. RULE: A peg riding the slider moves with it, allowing long-distance repositioning to set up jumps. TRAP: Assuming the slider moves only empty cells; forgetting it carries the peg wastes time on manual repositioning.

GOAL: Position the square so chains link three fixed anchors. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the square. RULE: Chains connect directly to anchors, ignoring obstacles. TRAP: Thinking chains must avoid water; they pass right through it.

GOAL: Move a plus shape to cover four scattered red dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the plus; Space cycles its shape. RULE: The plus must align perfectly with all dots at once, hiding none under the interface bar. TRAP: Assuming the plus stays visible when centered at the bottom edge; it vanishes under the HUD, blinding you to its position.

GOAL: Collect all colored items by covering them with the moving block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step; the bar depletes with each move. RULE: Each item collected rotates the target pattern; matching the pattern confirms progress. TRAP: Assuming a straight path works; precise steps are needed to hit exact grid coordinates, or you miss the item and drain the bar.

GOAL: Solve two color systems within six actions. CONTROLS: Click slots to move pieces; click tokens to switch systems. RULE: Moving one piece shifts the midpoint of its pair to the target. TRAP: Assuming slots are fixed; they shift, requiring dynamic tracking of current positions.

GOAL: Move the block to the red button, then to the exit, while managing ghost replays. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; ghosts repeat your path with a delay to toggle doors. RULE: Door states cancel out if a ghost and block occupy the same cell simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming a ghost is missing because it is hidden under the block; it is actually holding the door open.

GOAL: Clear the red barriers by firing a beam through the green square to refill your energy bar, then navigate to the exit dock. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your marker and set the beam’s direction; clicking keypad patterns expands your size or fires the beam. RULE: The energy bar caps at 64, so absorbing the green square before firing ensures you have enough power to destroy all red blocks. TRAP: Assuming zero energy is safe to move; acting with an empty bar causes immediate failure, forcing a restart.

GOAL: Ride the shifting bar to the far orange platform, then drop to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; yellow clicks advance the bar. RULE: The knob must stay on the bar; if it hangs in air, the click is refused. TRAP: Walking the knob ahead of the bar’s extension leaves it unsupported, wasting moves.

ESTABLISHED: The head must end at row 24 to attach the chain on row 25. R must be dragged from row 19 to row 25. FAILED: Moving the head to row 12 or 18 without dragging R breaks the chain. Approaching from above drags R to row 13, leaving it stranded. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the head on row 12 or 18. The win condition requires the head to be adjacent to the final block row. CONTROLS: Pressing DOWN moves the head down and drags blocks on the affected rows. Pressing UP moves the head up and drags blocks on the affected rows.

GOAL: Align two anchors so their midpoint falls on the target ring. CONTROLS: Click a token to swap its anchor; click empty space to move the slot. RULE: The square centers only when the average of the two anchor coordinates matches the target. TRAP: Assuming the white token was stuck; it simply needed swapping with the other anchor first.

GOAL: Press two buttons simultaneously to open the gate. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; Space records a ghost of your current path. RULE: Ghosts replay their exact recorded path every time you move, allowing simultaneous actions. TRAP: Recording a messy path first wastes time; plan the shortest route to the button before saving.

ESTABLISHED: The camera shifts vertically as the player moves, revealing a larger vertical space than initially visible. The map data is mostly consistent with this shift model, despite minor mismatches likely caused by HUD overlays or later-frame updates. FAILED: Attempts to map the upper world rows by assuming a static screen view failed. Trying to reconcile the initial frame’s open bottom rows with the later frames’ blocky appearance without accounting for the camera shift led to contradictions. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top of the initial screen view. The goal is not contained withi

ESTABLISHED: The player stands at (10,4). Two boxes exist at (10,11) and (6,12). A container is located near (9,4). The worker is active and moving independently. FAILED: Pushing the box at (10,11) left from (10,12) was not tested, but blocking paths made direct routes inefficient. Previous assumptions about worker drop zones were incorrect. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing all boxes to the container. The worker must also deliver its held box, and coordination is required. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. Space picks up or drops a box. The worker moves automatically toward the container when h

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while satisfying the box's shape and color conditions. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; standing on items consumes them to restore energy and update the legend. RULE: The legend must match the box's shape and color exactly, achieved by consuming specific items to alter its state. TRAP: Assuming the legend shape remains static; failing to consume the mystery object prevents the necessary shape rotation for a match.

GOAL: Move three blocks to slots, then ring them. CONTROLS: Click tip to swap active block; click source then target to move. RULE: A block moves only if the average position of all three stays on empty ground. TRAP: Assuming you can place blocks directly in slots; you must first group them to reach the slot's mean position.

ESTABLISHED: Basin three holds water below the wall segment. Basin two is empty. Water level is below the opening, so no flow occurs. FAILED: Pressing buttons near other basins did not trigger water equalization. Clicking the wall segment or the yellow gap produced no changes. GOAL IS NOT: Passive water equalization between basins two and three, or opening the yellow gap to create a passage. CONTROLS: Column buttons raise or lower water in specific basins. Clicking the wall segment or yellow gap has no effect.

GOAL: Navigate to the dock using the battery for energy. CONTROLS: Arrows move; clicks grow; yellow triggers teleport. RULE: Absorbing a full battery refunds energy, allowing growth. TRAP: Thinking partial battery overlap grants energy; it does not.

ESTABLISHED: Comet moves roughly four spaces per turn, tracking the nearest character. Merging happens when two characters touch. FAILED: Standing still while the comet approaches causes immediate loss. GOAL IS NOT: To outrun the comet forever; speed matters less than path efficiency. CONTROLS: Clicking a target square moves the selected character toward it. Prioritize creating distance from the comet before merging pairs.

ESTROLISHED: The grid is fully mapped and stable; no hidden panels exist beyond the visible wire limits. FAILED: Attempting to force a stalemate or isolate pegs failed because legal jump options always remained available. GOAL IS NOT: The objective is not to reach a zero-move stalemate or isolate a single peg through elimination. CONTROLS: Clicking selects pegs without scrolling the camera; sliders move panels but cannot exceed their fixed wire boundaries.

GOAL: Move the player to the target box to trigger the win condition. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one square in the chosen direction. RULE: The player must physically occupy the target square to complete the level. TRAP: Believing the path must be calculated instantly or that a single complex maneuver is required instead of simple step-by-step movement.

GOAL: Move the green peg to the target slot by sliding it across the board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the entire board; clicking a peg jumps it over adjacent neighbors into empty spaces. RULE: Jumps remove the jumped-over peg, so plan paths that capture multiple pieces in sequence. TRAP: Assuming board borders block jumps; they are visual only, and pieces slide freely across seams.

GOAL: Place two boxes into the goal zone using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the head; space drops the carried box. RULE: You can only carry one box at a time, forcing careful routing. TRAP: Assuming the helper robot will grab boxes for you; rely on your own placement instead.

GOAL: Move each plug across the central boundary so they occupy the opposite colored side. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the selected plug one step in that direction. RULE: A plug is only safe when fully contained within the background color of its new side. TRAP: Assuming any overlap with the target color counts as success; partial straddling fails the level.

GOAL: Rotate the arch around the block to paint the bottom half. CONTROLS: Click moves the arch along a path; Space confirms the position. RULE: The arch orbits the block, keeping its mouth pointed at the center. TRAP: Assuming all directions allow full rotation; the path is limited to specific arcs.

GOAL: Fill the grid with three specific color regions: a top-left triangle, a bottom strip, and a bottom-right triangle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piston into different poses; clicking selects the color; Space stamps the current shape. RULE: Each pose paints a fixed geometric region; correct color and pose combinations isolate specific areas without overlap. TRAP: Assuming the piston’s visible position matches the paint origin; the footprint extends beyond the cursor, requiring precise pose alignment.
